# Story 31 — Ticket History (Story: STORY-031)

## Prerequisites

- **Blocked by** `tickets/create-ticket` — the `Ticket` aggregate must exist in **Domain** with `Id`, creation metadata, and a persisted repository so `TicketId` lookups are possible.
- **Coupled to** `tickets/set-ticket-category-and-priority`, `tickets/assign-ticket`, `tickets/change-ticket-status`, `tickets/escalate-ticket` — each of those stories must **append a `TicketHistoryEntry`** using the writer this story introduces (`ITicketHistoryWriter`, see below). Coordinate the shape of the entry before merging any of them.
- Auth pipeline from Story `auth/user-login` completed — endpoints use `[Authorize]` and `ICurrentUserService.UserId` for attribution (`src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Common/Interfaces/ICurrentUserService.cs`).
- Scaffold state confirmed: `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/` and `Features/Tickets/` contain only `README.md` placeholders (no `Ticket` entity yet). This plan **defines** the history entity and read-side; it does **not** re-implement the lifecycle commands that will write to it.

---

## Story Goal

Expose a chronological, agent/supervisor/admin-visible **timeline** for a single ticket. The timeline aggregates every lifecycle event recorded against a ticket (creation, category change, priority change, assignment change, status change, escalation) with **who** performed it and **when**. Each event is emitted by the corresponding lifecycle command via a shared writer this story provides.

**In scope**

1. `TicketHistoryEntry` domain entity + EF configuration + migration.
2. `ITicketHistoryWriter` service (Application-layer contract, Infrastructure implementation) used by lifecycle commands.
3. `GET /api/tickets/{ticketId}/history` endpoint returning the timeline DTO.
4. Frontend hook + presentational **Timeline** component to render the entries on the ticket detail view.

**Out of scope**

- Writing entries from the lifecycle commands themselves (owned by the sibling stories; this story only ships the writer they call).
- Editing / deleting history entries (history is append-only).
- Full-text search / filtering / pagination beyond chronological ordering (creation → newest last, with server-side ordering by `OccurredAt`).

### 1 — Domain: `TicketHistoryEntry` entity + enum

```csharp
/// <summary>
/// Canonical set of ticket lifecycle events surfaced in the history timeline.
/// Extend only when a new lifecycle command needs to be represented.
/// </summary>
public enum TicketHistoryEventType
{
    Created = 1,
    CategoryChanged = 2,
    PriorityChanged = 3,

```

**Create file:** `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Entities/TicketHistoryEntry.cs`

```csharp
using CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Common;
using CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Enums;

namespace CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Entities;

/// <summary>
/// Append-only audit row describing a single change to a ticket.
/// Inherits <see cref="BaseEntity"/> so CreatedAt / CreatedBy are stamped by
/// AuditableEntitySaveChangesInterceptor; OccurredAt is the business timestamp
/// (may equal CreatedAt but is set explicitly by the writer for testability).
/// </summary>
public class TicketHistoryEntry : BaseEntity
{
    public Guid TicketId { get; set; }

    public TicketHistoryEventType EventType { get; set; }

    /// <summary>UTC instant the change occurred (set by writer, not the interceptor).</summary>
    public DateTime OccurredAt { get; set; }

    /// <summary>Identity user id of the actor; nullable for system-emitted events.</summary>
    public string? ActorUserId { get; set; }

    /// <summary>Snapshot of actor display name at emit time (denormalised for stable rendering).</summary>
    public string? ActorDisplayName { get; set; }

    /// <summary>Prior value serialised as string (nullable for Created).</summary>
    public string? OldValue { get; set; }

    /// <summary>New value serialised as string (nullable for delete-style events).</summary>
    public string? NewValue { get; set; }

    /// <summary>Optional free-text note (e.g. escalation reason). Max 1000 chars enforced by config.</summary>
    public string? Note { get; set; }
}
```

```csharp
using CustomerSupportCRM.Domain.Enums;

namespace CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Features.Tickets.History;

/// <summary>
/// Shared entry point used by every ticket lifecycle command

/// </summary>
public interface ITicketHistoryWriter
{
    Task AppendAsync(
        Guid ticketId,
        TicketHistoryEventType eventType,
        string? oldValue,
        string? newValue,
        string? note,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}
```

**Create file:** `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Application/Features/Tickets/History/GetTicketHistoryQueryHandler.cs`

- Signature: `Task<Result<TicketHistoryDto>> HandleAsync(Guid ticketId, CancellationToken ct)`.
- Verify the ticket exists via `IUnitOfWork.Repository<Ticket>().GetByIdAsync(ticketId, ct)`; throw `NotFoundException("Ticket", ticketId)` when missing.
  - If `Ticket` entity is not yet in the codebase (create-ticket not merged), guard with a `// TODO: replace with Ticket repository once STORY-... lands` and use a direct `DbContext.Set<TicketHistoryEntry>().AnyAsync(x => x.TicketId == ticketId)` fallback to at least return 404 when there are zero entries **and** no ticket. The executor must remove the fallback once create-ticket is merged.
- Load entries: `Repository<TicketHistoryEntry>()` with `TicketId == ticketId`, ordered by `OccurredAt` ascending, projected to `TicketHistoryEntryDto`.
- Return `Result.Success(new TicketHistoryDto(ticketId, entries))`. Empty entries (zero history rows) is **not** an error — the creation entry is expected to have been appended by `tickets/create-ticket` and its absence is a data bug, not a 404.

### 5 — API: controller endpoint

**Create file:** `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Controllers/TicketsController.cs`

```csharp
using CustomerSupportCRM.Application.Features.Tickets.History;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace CustomerSupportCRM.API.Controllers;

[Authorize]
[Route("api/tickets")]
public class TicketsController : BaseApiController
{
    private readonly GetTicketHistoryQueryHandler _getHistory;

    public TicketsController(GetTicketHistoryQueryHandler getHistory)
    {
        _getHistory = getHistory;
    }

    [HttpGet("{ticketId:guid}/history")]
    [ProducesResponseType(typeof(TicketHistoryDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
    [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
    public async Task<IActionResult> GetHistory(Guid ticketId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var result = await _getHistory.HandleAsync(ticketId, ct);
        return Ok(result.Value);
    }
}
```

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Non-existent ticket id** → `GetTicketHistoryQueryHandler` throws `NotFoundException` (see `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.Domain/Exceptions/NotFoundException.cs`), converted to HTTP 404 by `src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Middlewares/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs`. Frontend shows `ErrorState` with a "Not found" message.
- **Ticket exists but zero history rows** → possible only if the create-ticket command failed to emit its `Created` entry. Return `200` with an empty `entries` array; log a warning server-side. The frontend renders `EmptyState`, not an error.
- **Newly created ticket, only Created entry** → happy path for the second acceptance criterion; timeline shows a single item.
- **Deleted actor account** (`ActorUserId` no longer resolvable) → `ActorDisplayName` snapshot preserves rendering; if snapshot was somehow null, frontend falls back to i18n `tickets.history.system`.
- **Soft-deleted ticket** (`BaseEntity.IsDeleted = true`) → `IUnitOfWork.Repository<Ticket>().GetByIdAsync` returns null due to the global query filter in `ApplicationDbContext.OnModelCreating`, so the endpoint returns 404. Do **not** filter `TicketHistoryEntry` by `Ticket.IsDeleted`; the entries themselves are the audit trail.
- **Concurrent lifecycle commands** on the same ticket → two entries with the same `OccurredAt` are possible. Secondary ordering key: `Id` (Guid, monotonic-ish under sequential GUIDs) — reflect this in the query (`OrderBy(x => x.OccurredAt).ThenBy(x => x.Id)`).
- **Very long note / value** — enforced at DB level (`nvarchar(1000)` for `Note`, `nvarchar(512)` for values). Writer callers must truncate before calling; document in the `ITicketHistoryWriter` XML docs.
- **Unicode / RTL text in `note`** — stored as-is (`nvarchar`), rendered via MUI which respects the `dir` from `I18nProvider`.
- **Unauthenticated request** — blocked by `[Authorize]` at the controller; returns 401 from the JWT middleware (`src/BackEnd/src/CustomerSupportCRM.API/Extensions/JwtAuthenticationExtensions.cs`).
- **Enum serialisation drift** — see the note under Frontend Task 1: settle on `JsonStringEnumConverter` **before** merging so the TS union stays valid.

## Migration / Rollback

- Forward: `dotnet ef database update` applies `AddTicketHistoryEntries`. New table only; no data backfill needed because no ticket exists prior to `tickets/create-ticket`.
- Rollback: `dotnet ef migrations remove` (before deploy) or `dotnet ef database update <previous>` (after deploy). Because the table is append-only and referenced by nothing else at this point, a drop is safe.
- Half-applied risk: if the migration ran but the writer DI registration was missed, lifecycle commands would compile but fail at runtime resolving `ITicketHistoryWriter`. Guard by adding a startup smoke test that resolves the interface from the root service provider on `WebApplication.Build`.
